The rest have already been destroyed.|Echo|}} A '''T-series tactical droid''' served the [[Separatist Droid Army|droid army]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars]]. After the end of the war and the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], the Separatist [[battle droid]]s were decommissioned, and the rogue [[Cloning|clone]] [[squad]] [[Clone Force 99]], as well as [[Martez family|sisters]] [[Trace Martez|Trace]] and [[Rafa Martez]], both [[Mission to a droid decommissioning facility|attempted]] to retrieve the [[T-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid|T-series tactical droid]] for its intelligence before it was destroyed at a [[Decommissioning facility|facility]] on the [[planet]] [[Corellia]]. The two groups briefly competed to secure the droid's detached head, but eventually worked together against the facility's [[Imperial Police Droid|police droids]], reactivating the tactical droid to set the battle droids against their opponents. The tactical droid's head was destroyed during the skirmish, but the clones' leader, [[Hunter]], ultimately gave a [[data rod]] containing its intelligence to the Martez sisters in order to [[Clone Underground|fight]] the Empire. ==Biography== ===Decommissioned droids=== {{Quote|Tactical droid intel has tremendous value, which is why you're gonna break into this decommissioning facility on Corellia and retrieve one before they're all destroyed.|Ciddarin Scaleback, to Clone Force 99|}} A [[T-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid]] produced by [[Baktoid Combat Automata]] served the [[Separatist Droid Army|droid army]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] toward the end of the [[Clone Wars]] against the [[Galactic Republic]]. In [[19 BBY]], the Clone Wars ended with the Separatists' defeat and the Republic's [[Proclamation of the New Order|reformation]] into the [[Galactic Empire]].''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' With the end of the war, the Separatist [[battle droid]]s were decommissioned, and the [[tactical droid]] was set to be destroyed at a [[decommissioning facility]] on the [[planet]] [[Corellia]] in that same [[Standard year|year]]. The [[droid]] was to be saved from its fate, however; with the Republic's [[clone trooper]]s now serving the Empire, the intelligence tactical droids possessed regarding how to defeat them became valuable. Two parties [[Mission to a droid decommissioning facility|sought]] to retrieve a tactical droid from Corellia before the Separatist droids were destroyed: [[Clone Force 99]], a [[squad]] of rogue [[clone commando]]s operating as [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] for the [[information broker]] [[Ciddarin Scaleback]]; and [[Trace Martez|Trace]] and [[Rafa Martez]], [[Martez family|sisters]] working on behalf of former [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]],{{TBB|Battle Scars}} who wished to use the droid's data to [[Clone Underground|resist]] the Empire. In the facility, the tactical droid—partially disassembled, with its head detached but intact—was off-loaded onto the north end conveyor and sent on its way to be melted down. By the [[time]] that Clone Force 99 entered the facility, the tactical droid was the last such droid remaining, the others of its model already having been destroyed. After the [[Cloning|clone]] [[Omega]] had located the droid, Trace retrieved its head and ran, encountering the [[Clone trooper|troopers]] [[Echo]] and [[Tech]] as well as the squad's leader, [[Hunter]]. The intruders were soon discovered by the workers, who locked down the facility and dispatched [[Imperial Police Droid]]s. ===Unexpected allies=== {{Quote|What is happening?''"
"''Activate battle droids. Command them to attack all police droids.''"
"''Affirmative.|The tactical droid and Trace Martez, after the droid is reactivated|}} As the clones fended off the droids, Trace fled with the droid's head and threw it to Rafa, who dropped it onto a conveyor after colliding with a [[police droid]]. Both Trace and Omega raced to retrieve it, with the latter reaching the droid's head first and running off with it. However, when the facility was rebooted by the clone [[Wrecker]] and the conveyors began to move, Omega tripped and dropped the head, with Trace stealing it back. Trace soon returned to help save Omega, who had become trapped on the conveyor. [[File:TacticalDroidBadBatch.png|thumb|right|330px|The tactical droid was reactivated by Trace Martez and Tech in order to command the Separatist battle droids to fight for them.]] The two groups decided to put aside the fight for the tactical droid and work together to escape the facility. Wishing for a diversion, Trace intended to reprogram the tactical droid to command the deactivated Separatist droids. When Omega activated the droid, however, it was unable to transmit and powered down. Tech assisted by boosting the signal, also attaching a [[data rod]] to download the droid's intelligence, and the tactical droid reactivated. Following Trace's order, the tactical droid commanded the battle droids to target the police droids. With their adversaries distracted, the clones and the Martez sisters made their escape; however, the tactical droid's head was shot out of Trace's hands by the police droids and destroyed. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|Tech copied the tactical droid's intel to this data rod before it got destroyed.''"
"''Why are you giving it to us?''"
"''You'll use it for the right reasons.|Hunter and Rafa Martez|}} [[File:HunterRafaDatarod-Decommissioned.png|thumb|left|300px|Hunter gave the data rod containing the tactical droid's intelligence to Rafa Martez.]] After escaping the facility, Trace lamented having failed their mission, while Rafa criticized the clones for not knowing who Scaleback had intended to give the information from the tactical droid to. After Trace explained that their contact intended to use the information to fight the Empire, Hunter eventually provided the data rod with the droid's intelligence to Rafa, believing they would use it for the correct reason. Rafa later informed Rex that they had successfully acquired the droid's data as well as the rogue clones' assistance, while Scaleback was unhappy with her mercenaries' failure. When the clones protested their debt to Scaleback, she commented that retrieving the tactical droid would have been enough to make them even. ==Characteristics== {{Quote|New command sequence. Your target is factory security personnel.|The tactical droid commands battle droids|}} The T-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid, like others of its model, was part of the operational brains of the [[Confederacy military|Separatist military]], learning from experience in battle. It possessed the ability to command other Separatist battle droids. The tactical droid possessed [[Color|yellow]] [[photoreceptor]]s and plating colored blue and gray, standing at a height of 1.93 [[meter]]s. The droid primarily used the pronouns "it" and "its," but also the pronoun "he." ==Behind the scenes== [[File:CorreliaTacticalDroidConcept.png|thumb|right|230px|Concept art of the tactical droid by Stev Carey]] The tactical droid appeared, albeit unidentified, in "[[Decommissioned]]," the sixth episode of the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]]''{{'s}} [[The Bad Batch Season 1|first season]], released on [[Disney+]] on [[June 4]], [[2021]].{{InsiderCite|206|Star Wars: The Bad Batch Season One Companion|''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Season One Companion}} The droid was voiced by [[Liam O'Brien]]. Two pieces of concept art for the tactical droid were created by [[Stephan A. Carey|Stev Carey]] and dated to [[September 9]], [[2019]]—one featuring the droid entirely intact with a removable head and one of the droid's head after suffering damage.{{SW|url=decommissioned-concept-art-gallery|text="Decommissioned" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|Slides 2 and 9}} ==Appearances== *{{TBB|Decommissioned}} {{1st}} *{{TBB|Battle Scars}} {{Mo}} ==Sources== *{{SW|url=news/bad-batch-first-look-decommissioned|text=''Bad Batch'' First Look: "Decommissioned"}} *{{SW|url=series/the-bad-batch/decommissioned-episode-guide|text="Decommissioned" Episode Guide | The Bad Batch}} *{{SW|url=news/bad-batch-declassified-decommissioned|text=''Bad Batch'' Declassified: 5 Highlights from "Decommissioned"}} *{{InsiderCite|206|Star Wars: The Bad Batch Season One Companion|''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Season One Companion|reprint=1}} *{{InsiderCite|216|The Best of the Batch}} *{{SW|url=news/bad-batch-empire|text=5 Things ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Has Revealed About the Rise of the Empire}} *''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' *{{Databank|datarod|Datarod}} ==Notes and references== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of unidentified T-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid (Corellia)}} {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |ka=სერია T-ის უცნობი ტაქტიკური დროიდი (კორელია) |pt=Droide tático série T não identificado (Corellia) }} [[Category:Droids of the Confederacy of Independent Systems]] [[Category:Droids with he/him pronouns]] [[Category:Droids with it/its pronouns]] [[Category:Droids with unspecified gender programming]] [[Category:Separatist officers]] [[Category:T-series tactical droids]]
